bib.title: Reinforcement Learning: Industrial Applications of Intelligent Agents, Chapter 7. Learning All Possible Policies with Entropy Methods

question: How does maximum-entropy RL (soft actor-critic and relatives) produce robust stochastic policies, and how does it compare with PPO and with Q-learning?
contributions: Explains Shannon entropy, the maximum entropy objective, SAC, its discrete-action and automatic-temperature variants
Surveys extensions: other entropies, optimistic exploration, replay tweaks, soft policy gradient, soft Q-learning, path consistency learning
Compares SAC and PPO from published numbers (Table 7-1)
Grid-world demos of how entropy and temperature change exploration
Industrial example: SAC on the Donkey Car simulator with a VAE state, constrained actions

limits: Table 7-1 is a collage of numbers from different papers and implementations; author says researchers measure performance differently, rarely publish raw learning curves, and implementation details change performance.
Table 7-1 reports average performance only; it says nothing about stability across runs or whether training would continue to improve.
One column of Table 7-1 was estimated from published images.
The traffic case study is simulation only; the author notes no real-life results and doubts the policy network needs to be so complex.
Grid-world and Donkey Car demos are qualitative (figures and videos); no scores, seeds or error bars.
Written in 2020; predates LLM RL. SAC is for continuous (Gaussian) actions out of the box.
Author warns extensions do not guarantee better performance on your problem and results should be retested.
practices: Scan the temperature hyperparameter for each problem in plain SAC, or use the automatic-temperature variant (SAC Implementation Details; Automatically Adjusting Temperature).
Rescale rewards, because SAC is sensitive to reward scale relative to the temperature (SAC Implementation Details).
Anneal the temperature over time to explore early and become deterministic later (How Does the Temperature Parameter Alter Exploration?).
Oversample recent experience in the replay buffer and use a large buffer to limit catastrophic forgetting (Tinkering with Experience Replay).
Always retest algorithms and implementations on your own problem; published baselines may not match (Performance Comparison).
Separate vision from RL: pretrain an autoencoder and use the latent as the observation to cut training time (Minimizing Training Time).
Constrain the action space (limit throttle and steering) to stop training getting stuck (Dramatic Actions).
Pick the simplest solution that solves the problem and do not choose an esoteric algorithm over SAC by default, since industrial experience is greater (What Does This Mean Now?).
Use an exploration bonus in production for robustness, but avoid overfitting to the environment (Summary).
